name: Sara Kaba
sweep_summary: Sara Kaba [sbz] is not in the catalog. The single stress/prosody-titled bibliography item (Bardiaux 2013, regional prosodic indices in Belgian French) is a Glottolog machine misattribution — its record says language code 'Sara Kaba [sbz] (computerized assignment from \"perceptive\")' with language of publication French — so it is irrelevant (another language or variety, priority none). Pulling all 23 Glottolog records attached to sara1319 (saved as glottolog_sara1319_biblist.bib) shows 11 of them are the same kind of keyword noise ('perceptive', 'kabba'); the genuinely language-specific entries are Fédry, Danay & Ma.. 1981 'Initiation à la langue kaba (kyabé)' (CCL Sarh, print only — the best lead for a phonology statement on sbz, not obtained), Palayer & Solekaye 2004 'Dictionnaire démé' (sister language Kaba Deme), Moser's Kabba papers (Kabba is more likely Kaba [ksp] of Paoua than sbz), a 1935 wordlist, a 1931 melody sample and sociolinguistic surveys. Beyond the item list, I downloaded Keegan's open Sara-Bagirmi Project PDFs: the Kaba Na dictionary with English introduction (sister language kwv) states three level tones (high, mid, low) with tonal-change processes and never mentions stress; Keegan's Sara transcription note likewise gives three even tones for the Sara languages. No first-hand stress statement for sbz itself exists in anything read; no new stress statement was found. Semantic Scholar/OpenAlex APIs and HathiTrust refused, archive.org search returned nothing.

earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog lists 11 refs for Sara Kaba [sbz], none a grammar/phonology (only specific-feature articles, e.g. Moser 2005 on Kabba 'kare'); no stress description located.

new_statements.quote: Les langues SBB connaissent des systèmes à deux, trois ou quatre hauteurs tonales, dont les correspondances répondent à des formules spécifiques selon qu’on envisage noms ou verbes (Boyeldieu, 1988, 2000b). L’équivalence essentielle s’établit entre le niveau haut des langues à deux tons (modo, bongo) et le niveau moyen des langues à trois ou quatre tons (yulu, gula mere, ndoka, sar).
new_statements.translation: The SBB languages have systems of two, three or four tone heights, whose correspondences follow specific formulae according to whether one considers nouns or verbs (Boyeldieu 1988, 2000b). The essential equivalence holds between the high level of the two-tone languages (Modo, Bongo) and the mid level of the three- or four-tone languages (Yulu, Gula Mere, Ndoka, Sar).

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: statement check: another-languoid-suspected. extracted text of the HAL PDF we hold: 'ndoka' is listed apart from the 'langues sara' ('yulu, parlers gula, ndoka, bagiro, na, kenga, bagirmi, langues sara') and placed first under *SARA in the stemma. Glottolog 5.3 name search 'ndoka' (q2.sh) returns Lutos luto1241 (dialect Nduka nduk1240, Nduga-Luto branch, Ndele area, Nougayrol's field language) and not Sara Kaba sara1319 (Sara-Kaba < Barh Keita < Sara Peripherique). Boyeldieu & Nougayrol's ndoka is Nduka/Luto, so the 3-4-level statement belongs to luto1241. | checker: copies we hold (17 pp., text layer; the PDF's metadata gives the title 'Les langues soudaniques centrales: essai d'evaluation…
new_statements.relation_note: SBB languages have two-, three- or four-level tone systems; ndoka is named among the 'langues à trois ou quatre tons' (with yulu, gula mere, sar) whose mid level corresponds to the high of the two-tone languages (modo, bongo). Nothing on stress/accent.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Ndoka (Ndele Sara Kaba) is a level-tone language with three (or four) contrastive tone heights; Boyeldieu 2023 (cindex 2) restricts four-level systems to Yulu, Fer and Gula Koto, so ndoka has three levels (H, M, L). No word-stress statement.
new_statements.identity_note: Work's 'ndoka' = the 'sara peripherique' lect documented by P. Nougayrol (inedit 'Lexique ndoka') in the Ndele area of NE CAR: Boyeldieu 2006 (SBB presentation, held) maps ndoka immediately north of Ndele and lists it with wad, luto, nduga as lects of the CAR-Chad-Sudan three-borders zone; Nougayrol 1996 (quoted in Marti 2012, held) 'Sara peripherique (kaba-naa, ndoka, wada, bagiro..)'; Voegelin & Voegelin 1977 index 'Kaba Ndoko of Ndele'; this catalog's harvested alt names for sbz include 'Kaba Ndoko / ndoka'. Ethnologue/Glottolog Sara Kaba [sbz] = 'Ta Sara' of Ndele and Birao sub-prefectures; Glottolog has no separate Ndoka languoid (search 'ndoka' resolves only to Ndokama, a Basaa dialect). Hence very probably the same languoid; not the Kyabe (Chad) Sara Kaba Na [kwv] or Deme [kwg], which the same works list separately as na, tiye, kulfa, sime, 'dem. new_statements.relation_note: Group-level: eastern SBB languages have 2 tone levels, *OCC/'western' languages 3, and only Yulu, Fer and Gula Koto 4; Ndoka (a *SARA < *OCC language) is tabulated with noun tone patterns coded in the three-level system (11, 12=2, 22; 31, 32, 3-, 13, 33). new_statements.rule_in_words: Ndoka belongs to the 'western' SBB languages with three tone levels (High=3, Mid=2, Low=1); its noun tone patterns are given in that three-level coding. Nothing on word stress.
new_statements.exceptions: four-level systems only in Yulu, Fer and Gula Koto; two-level in eastern SBB (Modo, Baka, Bongo)
